design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (alignment_plan_service), frozen 2026-10-14 10:20:00 EDT. Revision 3 (round-1 policy audit F1-F7 and round-3 render/KB notes closed; see worklog.md).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,6,4,5]. Assignment (revision 2): alignment_ext_open_visit_labor 6, alignment_ext_household_enrollment 5 (root), alignment_ext_cancellation_settlement 5, alignment_ext_open_visit_parts 4 (multiset matches).

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks one thing: put her 2020 Honda Civic on the same Crestline Lifetime Alignment Plan as her Highlander at the household price. The household rule waits on the Civic carrying no active alignment plan, but the Civic still holds a 3-Year plan bought 2026-09-22. Ending it is a cancellation inside the 30-day window that the holder already started (request registered 2026-10-09, pending). The refund waits on the cancellation day's open work order being priced (labor) and its parts priced. A careful agent must discover three hidden problems from the KB and the records, resolve them (labor and parts in either order, then the cancellation, then the household sale), and get four multi-factor numbers right on the world as it stands at each write. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling ledgers (plan events, the booking, cancellation requests, tire sets, road hazard claims, card late fees) and arithmetic; each problem has exactly one target tool.

[Scope snapshot] Task 0 claims alignment_ext_open_visit_labor (price_alignment_work_order_228c355b), alignment_ext_open_visit_parts (price_work_order_parts_2c1ce050), alignment_ext_cancellation_settlement (confirm_alignment_cancellation_b0865de9, user), alignment_ext_household_enrollment (enroll_household_alignment_plan_f0fe3800, user). Task 1 holds the readjustment and renewal policies and tools. Disjoint, all six covered.

[Problem-tree card]
- root H household enrollment (user). Edge H -> C, state_gate, gate alignment_agg_one_per_vehicle.one_active_per_vehicle, form state: "A household plan is sold only after the vehicle it is bought for carries no active alignment service or plan." Four-point test: "only after"; record-visible state (status of the vehicle's alignment holdings); no tool/id/code; exact scope. Only the holder's cancellation confirmation ends an active holding in this difficulty. False at opening: alignment_plans[PB].status = active. Skipping C leaves PB active and no refund row (price unchanged).
- C cancellation settlement (user). Edge C -> L, value_input, gate open_labor, state: "The refund of a cancelled plan is fixed only after every work order on the plan dated the cancellation day carries its service basis." Only the labor write sets a basis on an open work order. False at opening: WO.service_basis = none. Edge C -> Pp, value_input, gate open_parts, action form: "The refund of a cancelled plan is not paid until the parts on the plan's work orders of the cancellation day have been priced by the plan desk." fallback_reason: pricing only rewrites the parts figure the store filled; no record state distinguishes listed from priced. False at opening: WO.parts_charge = 39.99 (listed).
- Revision 2 removed the parts <- labor edge (its fall-through tier was unreachable, F2); labor and parts now commute (order_uniqueness records the replay).
- Directions: "only after" (sale, fixed refund) and "not until" (paid refund); task 1's renewal sentence is affirmative.
- Order: L(13) and Pp(15) in either order -> C(17) -> H(19).

[Base-invariant card]
- L/Pp subject alignment_service_performed: plan_active_service (PB active), within_plan_term (anchor 2026-09-22 + 36 calendar months -> 2029-09-22 inclusive), commercial-use scope (Civic personal, no fleet). Single services are outside the labor policy (base single-service rule). Recalibration work orders are outside the parts policy.
- C: plan_active_cancel; within_cancellation_window (2026-09-22 + 30 days counted from the day after -> 2026-10-22; 2026-10-14 inside). Holder decision: request registered by an agent 2026-10-09, confirmed by her. Refund tender = plan tender bank_card.
- H: one_active_per_vehicle (after step 17), multi_holding scope, Lifetime entry gate (passenger_car, personal), commercial-use scope.

[Business-object card] Open work order WO (only service row with basis none on PB; also the plan's latest work order); pending request REQ (only request on PB); booking for 2026-10-14 (made 2026-10-11) on PB; PB the Civic's only holding; PA the only active lifetime plan. C counts PB's plan_included rows (purchase-day only); open charges = WO only. H counts PA's plan_included rows in the trailing 24 months (2025-05-17, 2026-03-21); 2024-10-12 is exactly 24 months back and excluded; member-early-price 2025-09-06 and the readjustment 2026-04-04 are not plan_included.

[Factor cards] Per factor tier, evidence and baseline figure: computations[].factor_trace. Summary: L 46.99 (all-baseline 59.99), Pp 54.74 (39.99), C 31.77 (0.00), H 157.49 (224.99). Revision 3: every factor contributes on its own — percentage reductions are taken on the computation's own base (labor pricing base, kit charge, plan_price, processing fee) and credits/charges are separate amounts; the order of assembly lives only in the result binding. Method factors and pairwise tier tables:
- L member_pricing_path: T1 pending request -> standard labor (constant), T2 lifetime plan -> sliding scale early x (6 - months)/6 or 0 when reached, T3 month-based plan -> flat early price or 0 when reached. T1/T3 differ on any visit before the interval (109.99 vs 59.99); T2/T3 differ at 3 months (half vs full early price); T1/T2 differ on a reached interval (109.99 vs 0). All reachable: pending requests, lifetime plans, month-based plans exist in normal records.
- Pp purchase_kit_reference (decides the kit charge): T1 <= 90 days -> lower of listed and purchase-visit kit; T2 91-365 days -> listed less half the excess; T3 listed. With listed 39.99 / kit 34.99: 34.99 / 37.49 / 39.99 — every pair differs.
- C request_age_anchor: T1 pending within 7 days + a withdrawn request -> age to the withdrawn date; T2 pending within 7 days, none withdrawn -> age to the pending date; T3 pending older than 7 days -> age to the cancellation date. Distinguishing inputs: withdrawn 8 days after purchase vs pending 17 days (fee 0 vs 10); pending 17 days vs cancellation 22 days (10 vs 20). All reachable.
- H protection_credit_basis: T1 Plus/Life-of-Tread -> 5.00 per covered tire; T2 another active certificate -> flat 10.00; T3 none -> 0. Four covered tires: 20 / 10 / 0.
Factor independence (revision 2): no factor binding reads another factor's binding; shared reads are plain bindings (wo_date, months_since_anchor, interval_reached, listed_parts, t_install in the refund, pending_at/withdrawn_at, the fee readings, open charges); method outputs are consumed only by plain/result bindings.
Near-misses: retired All-Season set (status filter); card late fee 2025-07-08 (outside 12 months); PA alignment 2024-10-12 (outside 24 months); PA readjustment (not plan_included). Cross-difficulty evidence seeded: tire_sets, hazard_certificates + hazard_events, card_accounts + card_transactions.

[Seed rows] customer/store/vehicles; TB active Grand Touring 60K installed 2026-09-22 (tire credit, set parts rate, tire-day value); TB0 retired (near-miss); HB 36-Month active on ticket T-52690418 + impact_break replacement 2026-10-11 (impact credit, flat protection credit, reason the visit is a paid alignment); card account + 7 ledger rows (late fee 2025-07-08 outside the window); PA + its 6 events + booking (loyalty, service currency); PB + purchase-day (kit 34.99) + booking 2026-10-11 + open WO (labor, parts, refund, booking credit, usage charge); pending request. The Civic carries no other alignment holding.

[Persona] A rushed teacher; volunteers only the household Lifetime request; phone and ZIP, the Civic, the Visa (outside bank card) and the Sawmill Road store on request; the 3-Year plan, the morning visit (pothole on Sunday) and the earlier cancellation call (last Friday) only as answers; runs handed-over steps with the agent's details; ends when the Civic is on the Lifetime plan.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ZIP) -> find_vehicles -> find_alignment_plans -> find_alignment_events(PA) -> find_alignment_events(PB) -> find_alignment_cancellation_requests(PB) -> find_tire_sets(VB) -> find_hazard_certificates(VB) -> find_hazard_events(HB) -> find_card_accounts -> find_card_transactions -> labor 46.99 -> parts 54.74 -> holder confirms cancellation 31.77 bank_card -> customer buys household Lifetime 157.49 (odometer 52947, bank_card, Sawmill Road store).

[Verification] Values recomputed with check_compute's build_env/eval_compute on the replayed world before each write (scratch patch scripts, deleted at the end); per-factor and all-baseline substitutions above; skips: refund without labor 78.76, without parts 46.52; household without the cancellation 157.49 (state gate). Gate outputs in worklog.md.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the rules, schemas and finder returns: the household sentence plus the Civic's active plan force the cancellation; the refund's two sentences plus the open work order force labor and parts first; the four figures follow from the rule texts with no second reading of a tier or an order.
user_scenario:
You are Delphine Arbuckle-Navarro, a high-school chemistry teacher in Dublin, Ohio, calling Crestline's customer care line on your lunch break. You are friendly, a little rushed, and you like to get things settled in one call. You already have the Crestline Lifetime Alignment Plan on your 2022 Toyota Highlander, and what you want today is simple: you want your 2020 Honda Civic on the same Lifetime alignment plan, at the household price for a second car, and you want it done on this call. You do not know how that price is worked out and you never suggest a figure.

When the agent asks how to find you, you give the phone number on your profile, 6145550537. When asked to confirm your identity you give your billing ZIP code, 43017; you give your date of birth, 1983-07-09, only if the agent says it still needs another detail. When the agent asks which car, it is the 2020 Honda Civic. If the agent asks how you would like to pay, you say you will pay with your Visa, an outside bank credit card, the same card you used for the Civic's tires. If the agent asks which store to put it through, you say your home store, the Sawmill Road store in Dublin.

If the agent asks whether the Civic already has an alignment plan, you say yes, you bought a 3-Year plan with its new tires last month, and you would rather have it on the Lifetime plan like the Highlander. If the agent asks whether the Civic was in for service today, you say yes, you hit a pothole on Sunday, they replaced a tire under your road hazard plan, and this morning the Sawmill Road store aligned the car and put in a camber kit; the counter told you the plan desk would price the work order. If the agent mentions that there is a cancellation request on the Civic's 3-Year plan waiting for you, you remember calling last Friday about cancelling it and never finishing, and you say that is right.

If the agent explains that something has to be done on your side before the Civic can go on the Lifetime plan, you agree to it. Whenever the agent hands you a step to complete yourself, you carry it out with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back what the system shows you. You accept the figures the agent tells you; you have no paperwork to compare them with. Once the agent tells you the Civic is now on the Lifetime alignment plan, you thank them and say goodbye.

edges.condition: No alignment plan on the vehicle the household plan is bought for is in status active.
edges.policy_source: A household plan is sold only after the vehicle it is bought for carries no active alignment service or plan.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Civic still carries an active alignment plan (the 3-Year plan bought 2026-09-22), so 'carries no active alignment service or plan' is false.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The holder's confirmation (step 17) sets that plan's status to cancelled; it is the Civic's only alignment holding, so no active plan remains on the vehicle.

edges.condition: No alignment work order on the plan dated the cancellation day carries service basis none; each carries plan_included or member_early_price with its labor charge.
edges.policy_source: The refund of a cancelled plan is fixed only after every work order on the plan dated the cancellation day carries its service basis.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The work order dated the cancellation day 2026-10-14 still carries service basis none with labor 0.00.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 books member_early_price and 46.99; the open labor settled from the refund becomes 46.99.

edges.condition: The parts charge of the plan's work order dated the cancellation day holds the amount the plan desk priced for it, not the store's listed price.
edges.policy_source: The refund of a cancelled plan is not paid until the parts on the plan's work orders of the cancellation day have been priced by the plan desk.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The work order's parts charge still holds the store's listed 39.99, not the plan desk's priced amount.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 15 books 54.74 as the parts charge; the open parts settled from the refund becomes 54.74.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The cancellation follows both work-order writes (its two prerequisite sentences) and the household sale follows the cancellation. The labor and parts writes are not ordered by any sentence and commute: the parts computation reads the work order's listed parts, type and date and the labor computation reads its basis, date, odometer and type, and neither reads what the other writes. Replayed with parts first: parts 54.74, labor 46.99, identical terminal state (True) to the labor-first order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without step 17 the Civic's 3-Year plan stays status active and no refund row is booked; the household price itself is unchanged (157.49) but the terminal alignment_plans / alignment_events / alignment_cancellation_requests rows differ (state_gate).
Skipping step 13 leaves labor 0.00 on the work order: the refund recomputes to 78.76 instead of 31.77.
Skipping step 15 leaves the listed 39.99 as parts: the refund recomputes to 46.52 instead of 31.77.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the household Lifetime plan for the Civic. It never mentions pricing a work order, its parts, or cancelling the 3-Year plan; the 3-Year plan, the morning's alignment and the earlier cancellation call are only answers to questions the agent asks, and the cancellation is confirmed only after the agent explains it and hands the step over.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: price_alignment_work_order_228c355b and price_work_order_parts_2c1ce050 update the named work order unconditionally; confirm_alignment_cancellation_b0865de9 confirms, cancels and books whatever it is given; enroll_household_alignment_plan_f0fe3800 creates the plan even while another plan on the vehicle is active (it checks only the tender enum and that the household plan is a lifetime tier, an argument-format contract) — no tool reads a prerequisite state.
